subproblems.title: Radial slicing bound: a radius t ∈ (R/4, R/2) at which the truncated integral ∫_{M∩B_t} θ⟨dβ, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is bounded by σ·sup|β|
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and Rp = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of S in U (IMRep U n with Rp.Represents S, i.e. S(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Let R ∈ ℝ with R > 0 and closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U, and assume ∂S(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0) (open ball). Then there are t, σ ∈ ℝ with R/4 < t < R/2 such that |∫_{M ∩ B_t(0)} θ(x)·⟨dβ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x)| ≤ σ·s for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ m) and every s ∈ ℝ with |β(x)| ≤ s for all x, where d is the exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv), ⟨dβ(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Rp.orient x (dβ x) and |·| is the Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (Rp : IMRep U (m + 1)) (R : ℝ), IsOpen U → 0 < R → closedBall (0 : Euclid P) R ⊆ U → Rp.Represents S → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U m, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ ball 0 R → S.boundary ω = 0) → ∃ t σ : ℝ, R / 4 < t ∧ t < R / 2 ∧ ∀ (β : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (s : ℝ), (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ≤ s) → |∫ x in Rp.carrier ∩ ball 0 t, (Rp.mult x : ℝ) * Rp.orient x (exteriorDerivative (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μHE[m + 1]| ≤ σ * s
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 4.6 and 4.9–4.11 for the Lipschitz function f(y) = |y|, chapter-06.txt lines 1335–1403). Simon's computation 4.11 (smooth increasing cutoff ψ of f, the Leibniz rule and ∂T = 0) and his integration 4.10 (monotone mass function, a.e. differentiation, here replaced by Fatou's lemma) are carried out directly for the truncated integral ∫_{M∩B_t(0)} θ⟨dβ, ξ⟩ dHⁿ = (S⌞B_t)(dβ), so neither the restricted current in B_R(0) nor the cutoff χ of the parent's step 3(b) is needed. Sibling used: covector_gram_bounds (accepted declaration covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds).

Notation. n := m + 1; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; (M, θ, ξ) := (Rp.carrier, Rp.mult, Rp.orient); μ := Rp.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, so μ(A) = ∫_{M∩A} θ dHⁿ for Borel A. For a k-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α (Euclidean coefficient norm) and ‖α‖ its operator norm. d := exteriorDerivative (= Mathlib extDeriv). B_r := ball(0, r). For β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and t > 0 put I_t(β) := ∫_{M∩B_t} θ(x) ξ(x)(dβ(x)) dHⁿ(x); the claim is that for some t ∈ (R/4, R/2) and σ ∈ ℝ, |I_t(β)| ≤ σ s whenever |β(x)| ≤ s for all x.

0. Facts.
(a) closedBall(0, R) is compact and contained in U, so by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult, μ(closedBall(0, R)) = ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,R)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_apply).
(b) If τ' = (τ'_1, …, τ'_k) is an orthonormal family in ℝ^P and α is a k-covector, then |α(τ')| ≤ |α|: sibling covector_gram_bounds (1) gives |α(τ')| ≤ |α|·(det(⟨τ'_i, τ'_j⟩))^{1/2}, and the Gram matrix of an orthonormal family is the identity matrix (orthonormal_iff_ite), whose determinant is 1.
(c) By the IMRep field orients and the definition IsUnitOrientationOf, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there are an orthonormal family τ(x) = (τ_0, …, τ_m) and a sign ε(x) ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(α) = ε(x)·α(τ_0, …, τ_m) for every n-covector α. By (b), |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for such x.
(d) For every smooth compactly supported n-form ω on ℝ^P the function x ↦ |ω(x)| is continuous with compact support, hence bounded by some s_ω. If moreover tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(0, R), then x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable, ω continuous), vanishes off closedBall(0, R) and is bounded a.e. by s_ω·θ·1_{closedBall(0,R)}, which is integrable by (a) and (c).

1. Cutoffs. Let g := Real.smoothTransition: g is C^∞, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 0 on (−∞, 0] and g = 1 on [1, ∞). Its derivative g' is continuous and vanishes outside (0, 1) (g is constant on (−∞, 0] and on [1, ∞), so g' = 0 on the open sets (−∞, 0) and (1, ∞) and, by continuity, at 0 and 1). Hence L := sup_ℝ |g'| < ∞ (a continuous function on the compact set [0, 1], zero elsewhere). For 0 < h < t define γ_{t,h}(y) := g((t² − |y|²)/(th)). Then:
(i) γ_{t,h} is C^∞ (composition of g with the smooth function y ↦ (t² − |y|²)/(th)) and 0 ≤ γ_{t,h} ≤ 1.
(ii) γ_{t,h}(y) = 0 if |y| ≥ t (the argument is ≤ 0), so tsupport γ_{t,h} ⊆ closedBall(0, t); and γ_{t,h}(y) = 1 if |y| ≤ t − h (the argument is ≥ (t² − (t − h)²)/(th) = 2 − h/t ≥ 1).
(iii) Dγ_{t,h}(y) = g'((t² − |y|²)/(th))·(−2⟨y, ·⟩/(th)). If Dγ_{t,h}(y) ≠ 0 then 0 < (t² − |y|²)/(th) < 1, i.e. t² − th < |y|² < t², and since t² − th > (t − h)² (because h(t − h) > 0) this gives t − h < |y| < t; in that case ‖Dγ_{t,h}(y)‖ ≤ L·2|y|/(th) ≤ 2L/h. Hence ‖Dγ_{t,h}(y)‖ ≤ (2L/h)·1{t − h < |y| < t} for all y.

2. Leibniz formula and pointwise bound. Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), 0 < h < t, γ := γ_{t,h}. The m-form γβ (x ↦ γ(x)β(x)) is smooth with tsupport ⊆ tsupport γ ⊆ closedBall(0, t). By exteriorDerivative_apply (Mathlib extDeriv_apply: dω(x)(v) = Σ_i (−1)^i D[y ↦ ω(y)(v̂_i)](x)(v_i), v = (v_0, …, v_m), v̂_i := Fin.removeNth i v) and the product rule D[y ↦ γ(y)·β(y)(w)](x)(u) = Dγ(x)(u)·β(x)(w) + γ(x)·D[y ↦ β(y)(w)](x)(u):
 d(γβ)(x)(v) = γ(x)·dβ(x)(v) + Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i Dγ(x)(v_i)·β(x)(v̂_i).   (2.1)
For x as in 0(c) evaluate at v = τ(x): since ξ(x) is linear, ξ(x)(d(γβ)(x)) − γ(x)ξ(x)(dβ(x)) = ε(x)·Σ_i (−1)^i Dγ(x)(τ_i)·β(x)(τ̂_i). Each τ̂_i is an orthonormal family of m vectors, so |β(x)(τ̂_i)| ≤ |β(x)| by 0(b), and |Dγ(x)(τ_i)| ≤ ‖Dγ(x)‖ because |τ_i| = 1. Therefore, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M,
 |ξ(x)(d(γβ)(x)) − γ(x)ξ(x)(dβ(x))| ≤ n·‖Dγ(x)‖·|β(x)|.   (2.2)

3. Use of ∂S = 0. Let R/4 < t < R/2, 0 < h < t, β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and s ∈ ℝ with |β(x)| ≤ s for all x. Since tsupport(γβ) ⊆ closedBall(0, t) ⊆ B_R ⊆ U (t < R), γβ is a test form in U whose topological support lies in B_R, so the hypothesis gives 0 = S.boundary(γβ) = S(d(γβ)) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply; d(γβ) is a test form in U by exteriorDerivative_isTestForm and tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset) = ∫_M θ ξ(d(γβ)) dHⁿ (Rp.Represents S). Both θξ(d(γβ)) and θγξ(dβ) are Hⁿ⌞M-integrable by 0(d) (their forms are smooth with tsupport ⊆ closedBall(0, t)). Hence, by (2.2) and 1(iii),
 |∫_M θγξ(dβ) dHⁿ| = |∫_M θ(γξ(dβ) − ξ(d(γβ))) dHⁿ| ≤ ∫_M θ·n·‖Dγ‖·s dHⁿ ≤ (2nLs/h)·μ({y : t − h < |y| < t}).   (3.1)

4. Letting h ↓ 0. Fix t ∈ (R/4, R/2). For k ∈ ℕ with k > 4/R (so 1/k < R/4 < t) let γ_k := γ_{t,1/k} and G_k(t) := k·μ({y : t − 1/k < |y| < t}) ∈ [0, ∞) (finite by 0(a)). For every y, γ_k(y) → 1_{B_t}(y) as k → ∞: if |y| < t then |y| ≤ t − 1/k for large k and γ_k(y) = 1 by 1(ii); if |y| ≥ t then γ_k(y) = 0. The integrands θγ_kξ(dβ) are Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (as in 0(d)) and, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, |θ(x)γ_k(x)ξ(x)(dβ(x))| ≤ s_{dβ}·θ(x)·1_{closedBall(0,t)}(x), where s_{dβ} bounds |dβ(·)| (0(d) for the smooth compactly supported form dβ), |ξ(x)(dβ(x))| ≤ |dβ(x)| by 0(c), and γ_k = 0 off closedBall(0, t); this majorant is integrable because ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,t)} θ dHⁿ ≤ μ(closedBall(0, R)) < ∞ (0(a)). So by dominated convergence J_k := ∫_M θγ_kξ(dβ) dHⁿ → ∫_M θ1_{B_t}ξ(dβ) dHⁿ = I_t(β). By (3.1) with h = 1/k, |J_k| ≤ 2nLs·G_k(t) for all such k. Put Λ(t) := liminf_{k→∞} G_k(t) ∈ [0, ∞]. If Λ(t) < ∞, choose a subsequence k_l along which G_{k_l}(t) → Λ(t); passing to the limit in |J_{k_l}| ≤ 2nLs·G_{k_l}(t) gives
 |I_t(β)| ≤ 2nL·Λ(t)·s   for all β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and s with |β(·)| ≤ s.   (4.1)

5. Choice of t (Simon 4.10 via Fatou). Put a := R/4, b := R/2 and ν := μ⌞closedBall(0, b), a finite (hence s-finite) measure by 0(a). For t ∈ (a, b) and k > 4/R the set {y : t − 1/k < |y| < t} lies in closedBall(0, b), so G_k(t) = k·∫ 1{t − 1/k < |y| < t} dν(y). The function (t, y) ↦ 1{t − 1/k < |y| < t} is the indicator of an open subset of ℝ × ℝ^P, so t ↦ G_k(t) is measurable (Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'), and Tonelli (lintegral_lintegral_swap) gives
 ∫_{(a,b)} G_k(t) dt = k·∫ L¹({t ∈ (a, b) : |y| < t < |y| + 1/k}) dν(y) ≤ k·(1/k)·ν(ℝ^P) = μ(closedBall(0, b)) < ∞.
Λ = liminf_k G_k is measurable (Measurable.liminf), and Fatou's lemma (lintegral_liminf_le) gives ∫_{(a,b)} Λ(t) dt ≤ liminf_k ∫_{(a,b)} G_k(t) dt ≤ μ(closedBall(0, b)) < ∞. Hence Λ(t) < ∞ for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) (ae_lt_top), and since L¹((a, b)) = R/4 > 0 we can fix t ∈ (a, b) with Λ(t) < ∞.

6. Conclusion. With this t and σ := 2nL·Λ(t) (a nonnegative real number), (4.1) states |∫_{M∩B_t} θ(x)ξ(x)(dβ(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ σ·s for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and every s ∈ ℝ with |β(x)| ≤ s for all x, and R/4 < t < R/2. ∎
proof_key_steps: Smooth radial cutoffs γ = g((t² − |y|²)/(th)) (g = Real.smoothTransition) equal 1 on B_{t−h}(0), vanish off B_t(0), and satisfy |Dγ| ≤ (2L/h)·1{t−h<|y|<t}.
Leibniz formula d(γβ) = γdβ + Σ(−1)^i Dγ(v_i)β(v̂_i) and the orthonormal-frame bound |ξ(d(γβ)) − γξ(dβ)| ≤ n|Dγ||β| Hⁿ-a.e. on M (covector_gram_bounds).
∂S(γβ) = 0 gives |∫_M θγξ(dβ)| ≤ (2nLs/h)·μ{t−h<|y|<t}; dominated convergence as h = 1/k → 0 bounds |∫_{M∩B_t}θξ(dβ)| by 2nLs·liminf_k k·μ{t−1/k<|y|<t}.
Tonelli and Fatou: ∫_{R/4}^{R/2} liminf_k k·μ{t−1/k<|y|<t} dt ≤ μ(closedBall(0, R/2)) < ∞, so some t ∈ (R/4, R/2) has finite liminf Λ(t); take σ := 2nL·Λ(t).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–3 of the parent proof (truncation of S_j at a good slicing radius: the IM restriction S⌞B_ρ of Simon Ch. 6, 2.9 for an integer multiplicity S, regarded as a current in ℝ^P). Siblings used: radial_slice (dtc_bc_tc_radial_slice_bound), imrep_restrict (accepted declaration rsd_cmr_imrep_restrict), imrep_current (accepted declaration dtc_imrep_current) and mass_equals_rep_measure (accepted declaration cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure). Notation: n := m + 1, Hⁿ := μHE[n], B_r := ball(0, r), M(X) := X.mass = X.massOn univ for X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. (Representation.) Since S is integer multiplicity, fix an IMRep Rp = (M, θ, ξ) in U with Rp.Represents S, i.e. S(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
2. (Good radius.) Sibling radial_slice, applied to U, S, Rp and R (U open, R > 0, closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U, Rp.Represents S, and ∂S vanishes on test forms supported in B_R), gives t, σ ∈ ℝ with R/4 < t < R/2 and
 |∫_{M∩B_t} θ(x)ξ(x)(dβ(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ σ·s for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and s ∈ ℝ with |β(x)| ≤ s for all x.   (2.1)
Put ρ := t. Then 0 < ρ < R, so B_ρ ⊆ closedBall(0, R) ⊆ U, and ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,R)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult (closedBall(0, R) is compact and contained in U).
3. (Truncated representation in ℝ^P.) Apply sibling imrep_restrict with U, U' := ℝ^P (univ), A := B_ρ (open, hence Borel) and θ' := θ. Its hypotheses hold: (i) M ∩ A ⊆ ℝ^P; (ii) θ is measurable (Rp.measurable_mult); (iii) θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M ∩ A (Rp.mult_pos); (iv) for every compact K, ∫_{M∩A∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,R)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (monotonicity of the set integral, M ∩ A ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ closedBall(0, R)); (v) for every x ∈ M ∩ A, δ := ρ − |x| > 0 and B_δ(x) ⊆ A (|y| ≤ |x| + |y − x| < ρ), so (M ∖ A) ∩ B_δ(x) = ∅ has Hⁿ-measure 0; in particular this holds for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ A)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_forall_mem, M ∩ A measurable). We obtain an IMRep R̂ in ℝ^P with carrier M ∩ B_ρ, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Consequently R̂.action(ω) = ∫_{M∩B_ρ} θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every n-form ω, and R̂.measure = (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B_ρ)).withDensity θ.
4. (The current.) Sibling imrep_current applied to R̂ gives Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with R̂.Represents Ŝ. Hence Ŝ is integer multiplicity and Ŝ(ω) = ∫_{M∩B_ρ} θξ(ω) dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P).
5. (Agreement.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ. Then ω is a smooth compactly supported form with tsupport ω ⊆ U, so by the definition of currentEval (the condition IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ U holds) currentEval(S, ω) = S(ω) = ∫_M θξ(ω) dHⁿ (step 1). For x ∈ M ∖ B_ρ we have x ∉ tsupport ω, hence ω(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and the integrand vanishes; as M is measurable and M ∩ B_ρ ⊆ M, setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero gives ∫_M θξ(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩B_ρ} θξ(ω) dHⁿ = Ŝ(ω). So Ŝ(ω) = currentEval(S, ω).
6. (No boundary inside B_ρ.) Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ. Then ∂Ŝ(β) = Ŝ(dβ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), where dβ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) has tsupport dβ ⊆ tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). By step 5, Ŝ(dβ) = currentEval(S, dβ) = S(dβ), dβ being a test form with tsupport in U. On the other hand β is also a test form in U (tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ ⊆ U); call it β_U. Its topological support lies in B_ρ ⊆ B_R, so by hypothesis 0 = ∂S(β_U) = S(dβ_U), and dβ_U and dβ are the same form (the same element of 𝒟ⁿ(U)). Hence ∂Ŝ(β) = 0.
7. (Mass comparison.) Let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Sibling mass_equals_rep_measure (for Ŝ with R̂ in the open set ℝ^P, and for S with Rp in U) gives M_O(Ŝ) = R̂.measure(O) and M_O(S) = Rp.measure(O). By withDensity_apply (O is measurable), R̂.measure(O) = ∫_O θ d(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B_ρ)) ≤ ∫_O θ d(Hⁿ⌞M) = Rp.measure(O), because Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ B_ρ) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono) and the lintegral is monotone in the measure (lintegral_mono'). Hence M_O(Ŝ) ≤ M_O(S).
8. (Finite mass.) By mass_equals_rep_measure with the open set ℝ^P, M(Ŝ) = M_{ℝ^P}(Ŝ) = R̂.measure(ℝ^P) = ∫_{M∩B_ρ} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,R)} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (step 2).
9. (Finite boundary mass.) M(∂Ŝ) = M_{ℝ^P}(∂Ŝ) is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(∂Ŝ(β)) over β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with |β(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (massAdmissibleOn univ m univ). For such β, ∂Ŝ(β) = Ŝ(dβ) = R̂.action(dβ) = ∫_{M∩B_ρ} θξ(dβ) dHⁿ ≤ |∫_{M∩B_ρ} θξ(dβ) dHⁿ| ≤ σ·1 by (2.1) with s = 1. Hence ENNReal.ofReal(∂Ŝ(β)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal σ for every admissible β, so M(∂Ŝ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal σ < ∞.
10. (Conclusion.) ρ satisfies R/4 < ρ < R/2 (step 2), Ŝ is integer multiplicity (step 4), and steps 5–9 are the remaining five assertions. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix an IMRep (M, θ, ξ) of S and take ρ ∈ (R/4, R/2) with the slicing bound of radial_slice.
(M ∩ B_ρ(0), θ, ξ) is an IMRep in ℝ^P (imrep_restrict) and represents some Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (imrep_current), so Ŝ is IM.
Ŝ agrees with S on forms supported in B_ρ(0) (the integrand vanishes off the ball); hence ∂Ŝ(β) = ∂S(β) = 0 there.
mass_equals_rep_measure gives M_O(Ŝ) = μ_{R̂}(O) ≤ μ_{Rp}(O) = M_O(S) and M(Ŝ) ≤ ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,R)}θ < ∞; the slicing bound gives M(∂Ŝ) ≤ σ.

subproblems.title: Weak sequential compactness of currents in ℝ^P with locally bounded mass (Simon 6.2.15)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, j ∈ ℕ) satisfy sup_j M_W(T_j) < ∞ for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with T_{φ(i)} ⇀ C (WeaklyConvergesOn: T_{φ(i)}(ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Bornology.IsBounded W → ⨆ j, (Ts j).massOn W < ∞) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), StrictMono φ ∧ WeaklyConvergesOn (fun j => Ts (φ j)) C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 3.11), whose subsequence part is "a consequence of the elementary 2.15" (chapter-06.txt lines 888–891). Simon's Lemma 2.15 (lines 318–331) is obtained from the uniform bounds sup_q M_W(T_q) < ∞ by "applying the standard Banach–Alaoglu theorem" to the functionals T_q. The proof below is that argument written out for U = ℝ^P: the sequential Banach–Alaoglu theorem for functionals that are uniformly bounded in the sup norm is proved by a diagonal subsequence on a countable sup-norm-dense family of test forms (steps 2–4), applied directly on the test forms (so the extension to continuous forms through the Riesz representation 2.7 is not needed). No sibling is used.

Notation. 𝒟ⁿ := 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ n; Λⁿ := Covector(ℝ^P, n) (a finite-dimensional normed space); for α ∈ Λⁿ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and ‖α‖ is the operator norm. Let N ≥ 0 be the square root of the number of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P; since |α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})| ≤ ‖α‖ (ContinuousMultilinearMap.le_opNorm, |e_i| = 1), |α| ≤ N‖α‖ for all α. B_k := ball(0, k) and K_k := closedBall(0, k) (k ∈ ℕ). B_k is open and bounded, so by hypothesis c_k := (⨆_j M_{B_k}(T_j)).toReal satisfies M_{B_k}(T_j) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal c_k for all j.

1. (Evaluation bound.) Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), W ⊆ ℝ^P, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ with tsupport ω ⊆ W, and s > 0 with |ω(x)| ≤ s for all x. The forms s⁻¹ω and −s⁻¹ω lie in massAdmissibleOn univ n W: their topological supports are contained in tsupport ω ⊆ W, and |c·α| = |c|·|α| (each coefficient scales by c). Hence ENNReal.ofReal(s⁻¹T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) and ENNReal.ofReal(−s⁻¹T(ω)) ≤ M_W(T) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn and linearity of T), so |T(ω)| ≤ s·M_W(T).toReal whenever M_W(T) < ∞. In particular, for every k and j:
 |T_j(ω)| ≤ c_k·s whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, tsupport ω ⊆ B_k, s > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ s for all x.   (1.1)
2. (Countable approximating families.) Fix k and let A_k := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ : tsupport ω ⊆ B_k}. The space C(K_k, Λⁿ) of continuous maps on the compact metric space K_k (with the compact-open topology, which is the topology of uniform convergence because K_k is compact) is separable and metrizable (Mathlib ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace: K_k is second countable and locally compact, Λⁿ is second countable). The restriction map r_k : A_k → C(K_k, Λⁿ), ω ↦ ω|_{K_k}, therefore has a separable image (a subset of a separable metric space is separable), so there is a countable D_k ⊆ A_k with r_k(D_k) dense in r_k(A_k). Consequently, for ω ∈ A_k and ε > 0 there is δ ∈ D_k with ‖ω(x) − δ(x)‖ < ε for x ∈ K_k, and ω(x) = δ(x) = 0 for x ∉ K_k (both topological supports lie in B_k ⊆ K_k); hence |ω(x) − δ(x)| ≤ Nε for all x. Put D := ⋃_k D_k (countable).
3. (Diagonal subsequence.) For δ ∈ D choose k(δ) with δ ∈ D_{k(δ)} and s_δ > 0 with |δ(x)| ≤ s_δ for all x (x ↦ |δ(x)| is continuous with compact support, hence bounded). By (1.1), |T_j(δ)| ≤ b_δ := c_{k(δ)}·s_δ for all j. Thus the points X_j := (T_j(δ))_{δ∈D} of ℝ^D lie in the set Π_{δ∈D}[−b_δ, b_δ], which is compact (Tychonoff, isCompact_univ_pi), and ℝ^D is first countable because D is countable. By IsCompact.tendsto_subseq there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and (L_δ)_{δ∈D} with X_{φ(i)} → (L_δ) in the product topology, i.e. T_{φ(i)}(δ) → L_δ for every δ ∈ D (tendsto_pi_nhds).
4. (Convergence on every test form.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ. tsupport ω is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport ω ⊆ B_k for some k ∈ ℕ, i.e. ω ∈ A_k. Let ε > 0 and put s₀ := ε/(3(c_k + 1)) > 0. By step 2 (with ε replaced by s₀/(N + 1)) there is δ ∈ D_k with |ω(x) − δ(x)| ≤ s₀ for all x. The form ω − δ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ has tsupport ⊆ B_k, so (1.1) gives |T_j(ω) − T_j(δ)| = |T_j(ω − δ)| ≤ c_k·s₀ < ε/3 for all j. Since (T_{φ(i)}(δ))_i converges, there is I with |T_{φ(i)}(δ) − T_{φ(l)}(δ)| < ε/3 for all i, l ≥ I. Hence |T_{φ(i)}(ω) − T_{φ(l)}(ω)| < ε for i, l ≥ I. So (T_{φ(i)}(ω))_i is a Cauchy sequence of reals and converges; define C(ω) := lim_i T_{φ(i)}(ω).
5. (C is a current in ℝ^P.) Linearity: for a, b ∈ ℝ and ω, η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, T_{φ(i)}(aω + bη) = aT_{φ(i)}(ω) + bT_{φ(i)}(η) → aC(ω) + bC(η), so by uniqueness of limits C(aω + bη) = aC(ω) + bC(η); thus C is a linear map 𝒟ⁿ → ℝ. Bound: if tsupport ω ⊆ B_k, s > 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ s for all x, then |C(ω)| ≤ c_k·s (limit of (1.1)). Sequential continuity (the field continuous' of GeometricCurrentOn): let ω_l → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges, i.e. there is a compact K with tsupport ω_l ⊆ K for all l and, in particular (derivative order 0), iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_l → 0 uniformly on K. Choose k with K ⊆ B_k. Given ε > 0, for all large l we have ‖ω_l(x)‖ = ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_l x‖ < ε for x ∈ K (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero) and ω_l(x) = 0 for x ∉ K, so |ω_l(x)| ≤ Nε < (N + 1)ε for all x, and the bound gives |C(ω_l)| ≤ c_k(N + 1)ε. Hence C(ω_l) → 0, and C ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n.
6. (Conclusion.) By construction T_{φ(i)}(ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, i.e. WeaklyConvergesOn (fun i => T_{φ(i)}) C, and φ is strictly increasing. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass bounds give |T_j(ω)| ≤ c_k·s for all j whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B_k(0) and |ω| ≤ s.
Separability of C(closedBall(0, k), Λⁿ) yields countable families D_k of test forms supported in B_k(0) that are dense in the sup norm.
Tychonoff and first countability of ℝ^D (D := ⋃D_k countable) give a subsequence φ with T_{φ(i)}(δ) convergent for every δ ∈ D.
Density plus the uniform bound make (T_{φ(i)}(ω)) Cauchy for every test form; the limit C is linear and bounded by c_k·sup|ω| on B_k(0), hence a current, and T_{φ(i)} ⇀ C.

subproblems.title: Federer–Fleming closure theorem in ℝ^P for degree n < P: weak limits of IM currents with locally bounded mass and boundary mass are IM (Simon 6.3.11 via 8.2, 8.3, 6.3)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with n := m + 1 < P, and let T_j (j ∈ ℕ) and T be currents in 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) such that every T_j is integer multiplicity, sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P (masses in [0, ∞]), and T_j ⇀ T (WeaklyConvergesOn). Then T is integer multiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), m + 1 < P → (∀ j, IsIntegerMultiplicity (Ts j)) → (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Bornology.IsBounded W → ⨆ j, ((Ts j).massOn W + (Ts j).boundary.massOn W) < ∞) → WeaklyConvergesOn Ts T → IsIntegerMultiplicity T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof cites Simon Ch. 6, Theorem 3.11 (Federer–Fleming compactness, chapter-06.txt lines 880–891), whose only non-elementary part is the present claim: "the existence of a T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) and a subsequence {T_j'} with T_j' ⇀ T is a consequence of the elementary 2.15; only the fact that T is an integer multiplicity current is non-trivial" (lines 888–891). Simon proves it in §8: Theorem 8.2 with Remarks 8.3(1),(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 2297–2473, printed pp. 176–179), Theorem 6.3 with 6.2 and 6.4 (boundary rectifiability; lines 1962–2003), the isoperimetric theorem 6.1 (lines 1939–1961), and Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 "⇐" (chapter-03.txt lines 107–300). Parts I–V below follow, with the citation labels adapted as explained in "Cited results", the closure/boundary-rectifiability argument written in this run for DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.closure_and_boundary_rectifiability-a1 (not reused by name: that node is unaccepted, reserved by another parent, and its statement also claims top-dimensional cases). Range correction (relative to that argument and to the first version of this proof): Simon's deformation theorem is stated only for n-currents in ℝ^{n+k} with n, k ∈ {1, 2, …} (§5 notation, chapter-06.txt line 1411), i.e. for positive degree and positive codimension, and it is cited below only in that range. Accordingly the closure statement CL(d) is asserted and proved only in ambient dimensions P' > d, and the boundary statement BR(d) only in ambient dimensions P' > d + 1 (Simon treats top-dimensional boundary rectifiability separately, by 3.14; that case is not needed here). Part II checks that the induction closes within these ranges, every application below states its range, and Part VI uses the hypothesis m + 1 < P exactly to place the stated case in the range of CL(m + 1). Departure (inherited from that reviewed proof): Simon's proof of 8.2 obtains rectifiability from the Rectifiability Theorem 8.1, which rests on the Besicovitch–Federer structure theorem (Ch. 3, 3.6), quoted in the book without proof ("For the proof of this theorem see [Fed69] or [Ros84]"). Here 8.1 is replaced by the tangent-plane argument of B. White (Comment. Math. Helv. 64 (1989) 207–220, cf. Simon's own remark in §8 that the structure theorem can be avoided), which uses only the slices, the lower density bound proved in Simon's 8.2 and BV-type estimates proved below; integrality of the multiplicity is then read off from slices (Step V14) instead of Simon's BV compactness argument. Errata: in Simon's 8.2 proof "Θ^{*n}(μ_T, ξ) < η" may be replaced by the lower density (only a sequence of radii is needed), and the support of the isoperimetric filling must be controlled (supplied by the deformation theorem); in Ch. 3, 1.6 the constant ε = 1/16ⁿ must be taken smaller (ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n}) for the contradiction in (10).

Notation. IM := integer multiplicity. Hᵏ := μHE[k]; Lᵏ is Lebesgue measure; ω_k := Lᵏ(B_1). For a measure μ, Θ^k_*(μ, x) := liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_k r^k) (open balls). M(X) := X.mass for currents in ℝ^P; |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors, and for k-vectors the dual norm. For currents X, Y in the same space, X + Y := X − (0 − Y). W ⊂⊂ U means: W open, closure(W) compact and contained in U (contract CompactlyContained). For d ∈ ℕ we use the two statements
CL(d): for every P' ∈ ℕ with d < P', every open U ⊆ ℝ^{P'} and all currents T_j (j ∈ ℕ), T ∈ 𝒟_d(U): if every T_j is IM, sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U (the boundary term read as 0 when d = 0, contract boundaryMassOn), and T_j ⇀ T in U (WeaklyConvergesOn), then T is IM;
BR(d): for every P' ∈ ℕ with d + 1 < P', every open U ⊆ ℝ^{P'} and every IM R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U, the boundary ∂R is IM.
Cited results. Three are siblings of this decomposition (comparator-accepted declarations reused verbatim); three are theorems of the source text, exactly as the parent proof cites Simon's slicing and compactness theorems.
(MR) sibling mass_equals_rep_measure (accepted declaration cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure): for IM X with IMRep R in open U, M_G(X) = R.measure(G) for every open G; in particular a nonzero IM 0-current has mass ≥ 1.
(IMC) sibling im_calculus (accepted declaration cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub): locality of approximate tangent spaces (a), IM restrictions (b), differences and integer combinations (c), and (d) for every IMRep the orientation satisfies |orient x α| ≤ |α| for a.e. x of the carrier, so that (R.measure, R.orient) is an admissible representation for (SL) and the integrals below are absolutely convergent.
(VO) sibling vanish_off_support (accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support): if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt S then S(ω) = 0.
(REP) Simon Ch. 6, 2.7–2.8 (Riesz representation of currents of locally finite mass, chapter-06.txt lines 265–282) with Remark 2.37(1) (absolute continuity, lines 644–652; for currents of top degree on an open subset of ℝⁿ, as in V11(c), absolute continuity is Remark 2.35, lines 606–638, which writes such a current with locally finite boundary mass as integration of a BV_loc density against Lⁿ, and Lemma 2.36 reduces the general case to it), valid in every ambient space and every degree (it is applied in ℝ^P and, in V11(c), in ℝⁿ): a current X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (U open) with M_W(X) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U has a Borel measure μ_X on ℝ^P and a μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable field ξ_X of k-vectors with μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ_X(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ_X(G) = M_G(X) for every open G, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α|, X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U); and if also M_W(∂X) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U, then μ_X(E) = 0 whenever Hᵏ(E) = 0. Consequences: |ξ_X| = 1 μ_X-a.e. (for open G, μ_X(G) = M_G(X) ≤ ∫_G |ξ_X| dμ_X); for a Borel B, X⌞B(ω) := ∫_B ξ_X(ω) dμ_X is a current (linear; sequentially continuous because |X⌞B(ω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_X(tsupport ω)), and for IM X with IMRep (M, θ, ξ) this is the IM restriction: by (MR) and REP, μ_X(G) = M_G(X) = (θHᵏ⌞M)(G) for open G, so the two locally finite Borel measures agree on Borel sets; both (μ_X, ξ_X) and (θHᵏ⌞M, ξ) represent X, so ∫⟨ω, ξ_X − ξ⟩ dμ_X = 0 for all test forms ω, whence ξ_X = ξ μ_X-a.e. (coordinatewise, a finite signed Radon measure on an open set annihilating C_c^∞ is zero).
(SL) Simon Ch. 6, 4.6–4.11 (slices by Lipschitz functions, chapter-06.txt lines 1335–1403): let U be open, X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U) and ∂X represented by Borel measures μ, μ' (finite on compact subsets of U) and fields ξ, ξ' with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ'-a.e., and let f be L-Lipschitz. Then X⌞{f < t}(ω) := ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and (∂X)⌞{f < t}(η) := ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' are currents, the slice Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} satisfies Z_t(η) = 0 whenever tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, M_G(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for every open G and t, and ∫⁻_{(a,b)} M_G(Z_t) dt ≤ L μ(G ∩ {a < f < b}).
(DT) Simon Ch. 6, 5.1–5.3 (deformation theorem, chapter-06.txt lines 1405–1930, statements lines 1428–1476, stated for n-currents in ℝ^{n+k} with n, k ∈ {1, 2, …}, line 1411; used here only in that range of positive degree and positive codimension; the dichotomy below is (1) in the proof of 6.1, lines 1948–1956, each k-dimensional face of the cubical grid of side ρ having k-dimensional measure ρ^k): for every P ∈ ℕ and every e ∈ ℕ with e + 1 < P (currents of degree k := e + 1, so 1 ≤ k ≤ P − 1) there is c = c(P, e) ≥ 1 such that for every ρ > 0 and every IM T ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with compact support and M(T) + M(∂T) < ∞ there are Q ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), R ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P), S ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with Q, ∂Q, R IM (Q = Σ_F β_F[[F]] with integers β_F over the oriented k-faces F of the grid of side ρ, so ∂Q is an integer combination of oriented (k−1)-faces), T − Q − S = ∂R, Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρ^k, M(Q) ≤ cM(T), M(∂Q) ≤ cM(∂T), M(R) ≤ cρM(T), M(S) ≤ cρM(∂T), spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ {dist(·, spt T) < 3√P ρ} and spt ∂Q ∪ spt S ⊆ {dist(·, spt ∂T) < 3√P ρ} (Simon's bound is 2√P ρ). (Parts I–V write "(DT) with m := e" for this choice of e, i.e. for currents T of degree e + 1, and verify 1 ≤ e + 1 < P at each use; (DT) is never applied to currents of degree P in ℝ^P.)
Measurable majorant (MM). In the situation of (SL) with G open and F(t) := μ_X(G ∩ {a < f < t}) (nondecreasing, finite if μ_X(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞), M_G(Z_t) ≤ L F'(t) at every t ∈ (a, b) where F is differentiable (a.e., Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt), F' is measurable (Mathlib measurable_deriv) and integrable on [a, b] (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv), and ∫_a^b F' ≤ μ_X(G ∩ {a < f < b}) (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc). For a sequence X_j with sup_j μ_{X_j}(G ∩ {a < f < b}) ≤ Λ, Fatou gives ∫_a^b liminf_j F_j' ≤ Λ, so for a.e. t: every F_j is differentiable at t and liminf_j M_G(Z_{j,t}) ≤ L liminf_j F_j'(t) < ∞.

Part I. Tools.
T0 (Zero current.) For every P, k and every U ⊆ ℝ^P, the zero current in 𝒟_k(U) is IM: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents it (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; the positivity, integrability, measurability and orientation fields hold vacuously because μHE restricted to ∅ is the zero measure; and the representing integral over ∅ is 0).
T1 (Compactness of Radon measures.) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and μ_j are Borel measures with sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, then a subsequence converges to a Borel measure μ on U, finite on compact subsets of U, in the sense ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dμ for f ∈ C_c(U); then limsup_j μ_j(C) ≤ μ(C) for compact C ⊆ U and μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(G) for open G ⊆ U. Proof: take compact K_k ↑ U with K_k ⊆ int K_{k+1}; by SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable applied to μ_j⌞K_k on the compact metrizable space K_k and a diagonal argument, Λ(f) := lim ∫ f dμ_j exists for every f ∈ C_c(U); Λ is a positive linear functional, so Riesz–Markov–Kakutani (Mathlib RealRMK.rieszMeasure) gives μ. The two inequalities follow by approximating 1_C from above and 1_G from below by functions in C_c(U) (Urysohn).
T2 (Restrictions converge.) Let X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_k(U) (U open), all with locally finite mass (representations from REP), μ_{X_j} → μ as in T1, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with μ({f = t}) = 0. Then X_j⌞{f < t} ⇀ X⌞{f < t}. Proof: let ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(U) with compact support C ⊆ U and ε > 0. The compact sets C ∩ {f ≤ t − ε} and C ∩ {f ≥ t} are disjoint; choose χ_ε ∈ C_c^∞(U; [0, 1]) equal to 1 on the first and 0 on the second. Then 1_{f<t} − χ_ε vanishes on C outside {t − ε < f < t} and has absolute value ≤ 1, so |X_j⌞{f<t}(ω) − X_j(χ_εω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_{X_j}(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}), whose limsup is ≤ |ω|_∞ μ(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}) (T1, compact set), and this tends to |ω|_∞ μ(C ∩ {f = t}) = 0 as ε ↓ 0. Likewise |X⌞{f<t}(ω) − X(χ_εω)| ≤ |ω|_∞ μ_X(C ∩ {t − ε < f < t}) → 0. Finally X_j(χ_εω) → X(χ_εω).
T3 (Cone inequality.) If X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), k ≥ 1, has finite mass, ∂X = 0 and spt X ⊆ B̄_r(x₀), then |X(ω)| ≤ r M(X)|dω|_∞ for ω ∈ 𝒟ᵏ(ℝ^P). Proof: let (Kγ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{j−1} ι_{x−x₀}γ(x₀ + t(x − x₀)) dt for a smooth j-form γ (the homotopy operator of the contraction h_t(x) = x₀ + t(x − x₀)); differentiation under the integral and Cartan's formula d ι_v + ι_v d = L_v for the radial field v(x) = x − x₀ give dKγ + Kdγ = γ − h₀^#γ = γ for j ≥ 1 (h₀ is constant), and |Kγ(x)| ≤ |x − x₀| |γ|_∞/j (|ι_vγ| ≤ |v||γ|). With ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equal to 1 near spt X: X(ω) = X(ζω) = X(ζ dKω) + X(ζ Kdω), and X(ζ dKω) = X(d(ζKω)) − X(dζ ∧ Kω) = ∂X(ζKω) − 0 = 0 by (VO). Hence |X(ω)| ≤ ∫|Kdω| dμ_X ≤ r|dω|_∞ M(X) (μ_X is carried by spt X, REP and VO).
T4 (IM is local.) Let U be open and X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with locally finite mass. If every point of U has an open ball B ⊆ U and an IM current X_B ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with X(ω) = X_B(ω) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B, then X is IM. Proof: let (μ_X, ξ_X) be the REP representation and (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B) an IMRep of X_B. For open G ⊆ B, the admissible forms for M_G(X) and M_G(X_B) coincide and give the same values, so by REP and (MR) μ_X(G) = M_G(X) = M_G(X_B) = (θ_BHᵏ⌞M_B)(G); two locally finite Borel measures agreeing on the open subsets of B agree on its Borel subsets, so μ_X⌞B = θ_BHᵏ⌞(M_B ∩ B). Both (μ_X, ξ_X) and (μ_X⌞B, ξ_B) represent X on forms supported in B, so ∫⟨ω, ξ_X − ξ_B⟩ dμ_X = 0 for every test form ω supported in B; coordinatewise (a finite signed Radon measure on an open set annihilating C_c^∞ is zero: approximate indicators of compact sets by smooth functions and use dominated convergence and inner regularity) ξ_X = ξ_B μ_X-a.e. on B. Cover U by countably many such balls B_i, put A_i := B_i ∖ ⋃_{l<i} B_l and M := ⋃_i (M_{B_i} ∩ A_i), θ := θ_{B_i}, ξ := ξ_{B_i} on M_{B_i} ∩ A_i. Then X(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHᵏ; the IMRep fields hold (countable unions of rectifiable sets are rectifiable; θ ≥ 1 integer-valued; ∫_{M∩K}θ dHᵏ = μ_X(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; by IMC(a), for a.e. x ∈ M ∩ A_i the approximate tangent spaces of M, of M ∩ A_i = M_{B_i} ∩ A_i and of M_{B_i} coincide, and ξ_{B_i}(x) orients them).
T5 (Dilations.) For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := λ⁻¹(y − a) and η_#X := the push-forward by this proper affine map (SimonGMT affinePushforward): η_#X(ω) = X(η^#ω), (η^#ω)(y) = λ^{−k}ω(η(y)) (as k-covectors). Then ∂η_# = η_#∂, M_{η(W)}(η_#X) = λ^{−k}M_W(X), spt η_#X = η(spt X); if X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is IM then η_#X = τ(η(M), θ ∘ η⁻¹, ξ ∘ η⁻¹) is IM (Hᵏ(η(A)) = λ^{−k}Hᵏ(A), and the approximate tangent space of η(M) at η(x) is that of M at x because blow-ups commute: η_{η(x),r}(η(M)) = η_{x,λr}(M)); restrictions commute: η_#(X⌞{f ∘ η < t}) = (η_#X)⌞{f < t} (by the change of variables η_#X(ω) = ∫⟨λ^{−k}ω(η(x)), ξ_X(x)⟩ dμ_X(x), the pair (λ^{−k}η_*μ_X, ξ_X ∘ η⁻¹) represents η_#X, and restrictions do not depend on the representation by (o) of V4).

Part II. Structure of the induction. CL(d) and BR(d) are as defined in the Notation paragraph, each with its range of ambient dimensions; the ambient space of Parts III–V is denoted ℝ^P. We prove CL(0) in every ambient dimension P ≥ 1 (Part III). For every d ≥ 0 we prove BR(d) in every ambient dimension P ≥ d + 2 from CL(d) (Part IV), and CL(d+1) in every ambient dimension P ≥ d + 2 from CL(d) and BR(d) (Part V). The ranges close up. Part IV works in ℝ^P with d + 1 < P and uses CL(d) only in ℝ^P (d < P) and (DT) only in degree d + 1 ∈ [1, P − 1]. Part V proves CL(n), n := d + 1, in ℝ^P with n < P. It uses BR(d) only for n-currents in open subsets of ℝ^P (d + 1 = n < P), CL(d) only for (n−1)-currents in open subsets of ℝ^P (d < P), and (DT) only through (Iso), in degree d = n − 1 ∈ [1, P − 1] when n ≥ 2. By induction on d, for every d ∈ ℕ, CL(d) holds in every ambient dimension P > d and BR(d) in every ambient dimension P > d + 1. No top-dimensional case (currents of degree P in ℝ^P) of CL, BR or (DT) is used. The only top-dimensional objects are the n-currents Y_k on an open subset of ℝⁿ in V11, and only (REP) is applied to them (Simon 2.35 covers that case).

Part III. CL(0) (in every ambient dimension P ≥ 1; the argument does not use the range). Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open and T_j ∈ 𝒟_0(U) be IM with sup_j M_W(T_j) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U (the boundary term is 0 in degree 0) and T_j ⇀ T. In degree 0, H⁰ is counting measure and an IMRep is a set M_j with θ_j ≥ 1 and orientations ±1 (the approximate tangent space at each point of a locally finite set is {0}); local integrability makes M_j ∩ K finite for compact K ⊆ U, so T_j(a) = Σ_{x∈M_j} m_j(x) a(x) with m_j(x) ∈ ℤ ∖ {0} (a ∈ C_c^∞(U) a 0-form). T has locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity). Fix x₀ ∈ U and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x₀) ⊆ U, and c := sup_j M_{B_{2r}(x₀)}(T_j) < ∞; by (MR), Σ_{x∈M_j∩B_{2r}(x₀)}|m_j(x)| ≤ c, so on B_{2r}(x₀), T_j = Σ_{i=1}^{N_j} ε_{j,i}δ_{x_{j,i}} with N_j ≤ c, ε_{j,i} = ±1, x_{j,i} ∈ B_{2r}(x₀) (points repeated by multiplicity). Pass to a subsequence with N_j = N, ε_{j,i} = ε_i and x_{j,i} → y_i ∈ B̄_{2r}(x₀). For a ∈ C_c^∞(B_r(x₀)), T(a) = lim_j Σ_i ε_i a(x_{j,i}) = Σ_i ε_i a(y_i). So on B_r(x₀), T agrees with the IM current Σ_{y} m(y)δ_y, m(y) := Σ_{y_i = y}ε_i (points with m(y) = 0 omitted; finite carrier in U). By T4, T is IM.

Part IV. BR(d) from CL(d). Let P ≥ d + 2 (i.e. d + 1 < P), U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) IM with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U. CL(d) is available in ℝ^P because d < P.
1. (Localization.) Fix x₀ ∈ U and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U; f := |· − x₀|. Apply (SL) to R (IM representation) and ∂R (REP representation); by (MM), for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀) the slice Z_r := ∂(R⌞B_r(x₀)) − (∂R)⌞B_r(x₀) has finite mass. Fix such r. (The total mass of Z_r is controlled by its mass in G := B_{r₀}(x₀): Z_r vanishes on forms supported off ∂B_r(x₀) ⊆ G, so splitting an admissible form ω = χω + (1 − χ)ω with χ ∈ C_c^∞(G; [0,1]) equal to 1 near ∂B_r(x₀) gives Z_r(ω) = Z_r(χω) ≤ M_G(Z_r).) R' := R⌞B_r(x₀) is IM (IMC(b)) with carrier contained in B_r(x₀), supported in B̄_r(x₀), M(R') < ∞ (MR), and ∂R' = (∂R)⌞B_r(x₀) + Z_r has finite mass. Extend R' to ℝ^P: R̂'(ω) := R'(ζω) with ζ ∈ C_c^∞(U) equal to 1 near B̄_r(x₀) (independent of ζ by VO); R̂' is IM with the same IMRep, M(R̂') = M(R'), ∂R̂' = (∂R')^ (VO).
2. (Approximation by the deformation theorem; Simon 6.2.) R̂' is an IM current of degree d + 1 with 1 ≤ d + 1 < P, compact support in B̄_r(x₀) and M(R̂') + M(∂R̂') < ∞, so (DT) applies in its range. By (DT) with m := d and ρ := ρ_k := 2^{−k}, applied to R̂': R̂' − Q_k − S_k = ∂R_k with Q_k and ∂Q_k IM, M(R_k) ≤ cρ_kM(R̂') → 0, M(S_k) ≤ cρ_kM(∂R̂') → 0, M(∂Q_k) ≤ cM(∂R̂'), and spt Q_k ⊆ {dist(·, B̄_r(x₀)) < 3√P ρ_k}. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P), |Q_k(ω) − R̂'(ω)| ≤ M(S_k)|ω|_∞ + M(R_k)|dω|_∞ → 0, so Q_k ⇀ R̂' and ∂Q_k ⇀ ∂R̂'. The ∂Q_k are IM d-currents in ℝ^P with ∂∂Q_k = 0 and bounded masses, so by CL(d) (in U := ℝ^P, within its range since d < P; the boundary term is M(∂∂Q_k) = 0, or 0 in degree 0), ∂R̂' is IM.
3. (Back to ∂R.) If tsupport η ⊆ B_r(x₀), then ∂R̂'(η) = (∂R)⌞B_r(x₀)(η) + Z_r(η) = ∂R(η) + 0 (η vanishes off B_r(x₀); Z_r(η) = 0 by SL since tsupport η misses {f = r}). The restriction of ∂R̂' to test forms in U is IM: by (MR) and (VO) its IMRep measure vanishes off spt ∂R̂' ⊆ B̄_r(x₀) ⊆ U, so the carrier can be intersected with B̄_r(x₀) without changing the current (IMC(b)), and the resulting data form an IMRep in U. By T4 (∂R has locally finite mass by hypothesis), ∂R is IM. ∎

Part V. CL(n) for n = d + 1 ≥ 1, assuming CL(d) (in every ambient dimension > d) and BR(d) (in every ambient dimension > d + 1).
Let P > n (i.e. d + 1 < P), U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(U) IM, Λ_W := sup_j (M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, T_j ⇀ T. Throughout Part V the ambient space is this ℝ^P with n < P. So every application of BR(d) below (to n-currents in open subsets of ℝ^P) is in its range d + 1 = n < P. Every application of CL(d) (to (n−1)-currents in open subsets of ℝ^P) is in its range d < P. (DT) enters only through (Iso), in degree n − 1 with 1 ≤ n − 1 < P.
V1 (Boundaries.) Each ∂T_j is IM by BR(d) (in U ⊆ ℝ^P; range d + 1 = n < P). T and ∂T have locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity), hence representations (REP).
V2 (Localization; Simon 8.3(1).) Fix x₀ ∈ U, r₀ > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U. Pass to a subsequence with μ_{T_j} → μ on U (T1). By (SL) with f := |· − x₀| (representations from IMReps of T_j and ∂T_j, with |orient| ≤ 1 a.e. by IMC(d)) and (MM) (with Λ_{B_{r₀}(x₀)}; total masses of the slices are controlled by their masses in B_{r₀}(x₀) as in IV.1), for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀), liminf_j M(Z_{j,r}) < ∞, where Z_{j,r} := ∂(T_j⌞B_r(x₀)) − (∂T_j)⌞B_r(x₀); also μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0 for all but countably many r. Fix such r and pass to a subsequence with sup_j M(Z_{j,r}) < ∞. Then T'_j := T_j⌞B_r(x₀) are IM (IMC(b)), supported in K := B̄_r(x₀), with sup_j (M(T'_j) + M(∂T'_j)) < ∞, and T'_j ⇀ T⌞B_r(x₀) (T2). Extending to ℝ^P as in IV.1 (carriers inside B_r(x₀)), the extensions T̂'_j are IM with M(∂T̂'_j) = M(∂T'_j) < ∞, so ∂T̂'_j is IM by BR(d) applied in ℝ^P (range n < P); and T̂'_j ⇀ (T⌞B_r(x₀))^. Then the claim (CL*) below shows that (T⌞B_r(x₀))^ is IM; its restriction to U is IM and agrees with T on forms supported in B_r(x₀). By T4, T is IM. It remains to prove:
(CL*) (Here n < P.) If T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) are IM, ∂T_j are IM, spt T_j ⊆ K (a fixed compact set), sup_j (M(T_j) + M(∂T_j)) < ∞ and T_j ⇀ T, then T is IM.
V3 (Reduction to cycles; Simon 8.2 and White.) In (CL*), ∂T_j are IM (n−1)-cycles supported in K with bounded masses and ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T, so ∂T is IM by CL(d) (in ℝ^P; range d < P), with spt ∂T ⊆ K, M(∂T) < ∞ and ∂∂T = 0 (if n − 1 ≥ 1). We find an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with compact support and ∂Y = ∂T:
(Iso) If n − 1 = d ≥ 1 (so 1 ≤ d < n < P) and Z ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) is an IM cycle with compact support, then there is IM Y with ∂Y = Z, M(Y) ≤ c_I M(Z)^{(d+1)/d} and spt Y ⊆ {dist(·, spt Z) < 3√P(2c M(Z))^{1/d}}, where c = c(P, d − 1) is the constant of (DT) and c_I := c(2c)^{1/d}. Proof (Simon 6.1, stated for (n−1)-cycles in ℝ^{n+k} with n ≥ 2 and k ≥ 1, i.e. here d + 1 ≥ 2 and d + 1 < P; its proof uses (DT) only in degree d, and 1 ≤ d < P): if Z = 0 take Y = 0 (IM by T0). Otherwise apply (DT) with m := d − 1 (degree d, within its range 1 ≤ d < P) and ρ := (2cM(Z))^{1/d} to Z (IM, compact support, M(Z) + M(∂Z) = M(Z) < ∞): Z − Q − S = ∂Y with M(S) ≤ cρM(∂Z) = 0, so S = 0; M(Q) ≤ cM(Z) = ρ^d/2 < ρ^d, so Q = 0 by the dichotomy Q = 0 ∨ M(Q) ≥ ρ^d; hence Z = ∂Y with Y IM, M(Y) ≤ cρM(Z) = c_IM(Z)^{(d+1)/d} and the support bound of (DT).
If n = 1: ∂T is an IM 0-current with compact support, so ∂T = Σ_{i=1}^N m_iδ_{x_i}; with ζ ∈ C_c^∞ equal to 1 near K, ∂T(ζ) = lim_j T_j(dζ) = 0 (VO), i.e. Σm_i = 0; let Y := Σ_i m_i[[x₀, x_i]] (oriented segments from a fixed point x₀ ∉ {x_1, …, x_N}; each is IM — carrier the open segment, multiplicity 1, unit tangent orientation, approximate tangent line at every interior point — and integer combinations are IM by IMC(c)); then ∂Y = Σ m_i(δ_{x_i} − δ_{x₀}) = ∂T.
Put Γ := T − Y. Then Γ is a cycle (∂Γ = ∂T − ∂Y = 0) with compact support (⊆ K ∪ spt Y) and finite mass, and it suffices to show that Γ is IM, because then T = Γ − (0 − Y) is IM (IMC(c)). (Note that the currents T_j − Y are not cycles; the argument below only uses properties of the limit.)
V4 (IM slice property.) For a current X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that X and ∂X have locally finite mass (if n = 1, ∂X is a 0-current and terms involving ∂∂X are absent), with REP representations of X and ∂X, a Lipschitz f and t ∈ ℝ, let ⟨X, f, t⟩ := ∂(X⌞{f < t}) − (∂X)⌞{f < t} (the current Z_t of SL). Say that X has (ISP) if for every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ and L¹-a.e. t, ⟨X, f, t⟩ is IM. For a cycle, ⟨X, f, t⟩ = ∂(X⌞{f < t}).
(o) Linearity. For such X, X' and Borel B, (X − X')⌞B = X⌞B − X'⌞B: the finite-dimensional-vector-valued Radon measures ξ_{X−X'}μ_{X−X'} and ξ_Xμ_X − ξ_{X'}μ_{X'} integrate every smooth compactly supported covector field in the same way, hence (coordinatewise, a finite signed Radon measure on an open set annihilating C_c^∞ is zero: approximate indicators of compact sets by smooth functions and use dominated convergence and inner regularity) agree on bounded Borel sets. Consequently ⟨X − X', f, t⟩ = ⟨X, f, t⟩ − ⟨X', f, t⟩.

A1. The condition dim Q = n is part of the hypothesis.
A2. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ). Its support is compact, so there is R₀ ≥ 0 with f(z) = 0 whenever |z| > R₀. For λ > 0 the map η_λ is an affine homeomorphism, so η_λ(M) and η_λ(M') are Borel; by injectivity η_λ(M) ∖ η_λ(M') = η_λ(M ∖ M').

subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of U (Simon 6.3.1 data). Then there is T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R.Represents T). Here T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means a GeometricCurrentOn U n: a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with T(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges).

Source: Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753), where formula (‡) is asserted to define a current. The parent proof uses this in step 6.6 for X̃ = τ(M_X ∩ K, θ_X, ξ_X) in U.
Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M; for a covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map.
1. Unit orientations have norm at most one. By the field orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) such that ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Then for every covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ₁, …, τₙ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ|τᵢ| = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the product is empty when n = 0).
2. Measurability. For every continuous n-form ω, the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Indeed θ is measurable (ℕ-valued), ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), ω is continuous, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous because it is bounded bilinear (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply; Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
3. θ is integrable over compact sets. Let K be compact with K ⊆ U. Then 1_K θ is μ-integrable: it is measurable, and ∫ 1_K θ dμ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult, since (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict; integrable_indicator_iff). Write C_K := ∫ 1_K θ dμ ∈ [0, ∞).
4. Integrability of the integrand. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), K := tsupport ω (compact, ⊆ U), and B := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B·1_K(x)θ(x); if x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0. By steps 2–3 and domination (Integrable.mono'), x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable.
5. Linearity. Define T(ω) := R.action ω for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Each ξ(x) is linear, so the integrand for ω + η is the sum of the integrands for ω and η. Both are integrable by step 4, so T(ω + η) = T(ω) + T(η) (integral_add). The integrand for cω is c times the integrand for ω, so T(cω) = cT(ω) (integral_const_mul). Thus T is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U), and R.Represents T holds by definition.
6. Sequential continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and every derivative converges uniformly on K. For the 0-th derivative (‖D⁰g(x)‖ = ‖g(x)‖ and D⁰0 = 0) this says ε_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ ε_j·1_K(x)θ(x), since ω_j(x) = 0 off K. Hence |T(ω_j)| ≤ ε_j·C_K (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with step 3). Given ε > 0, choose N such that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε/(C_K + 1) for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K. Then |T(ω_j)| ≤ εC_K/(C_K + 1) < ε for j ≥ N, so T(ω_j) → 0.
7. By steps 5 and 6, T is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unit orientations satisfy |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for a.e. x in M.
For a test form ω the integrand is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by sup|ω|·1_{spt ω}·θ, which is integrable by local integrability of θ. Hence ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is linear.
If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with supports in a compact K, then |T(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K|ω_j|·∫_{M∩K} θ → 0, so T is a current.

Write E for the space of n-covectors on ℝ^P with the inner product ⟨α, α'⟩_E := Σ_I α(e_I) α'(e_I) (sum over increasing n-tuples I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n), e_I := (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})); its norm is |·|. If n > P then E = 0, every n-form vanishes, so T = 0 and M_W(T) = 0, and Hⁿ = 0 on ℝ^P (Hausdorff dimension P < n), so μ_R = 0 and the claim holds. Assume n ≤ P.
1. (Algebra.) Let τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P be orthonormal and let A be the n×P matrix A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩. Expanding each τ_i in the standard basis, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I), where A_I is the n×n submatrix of A with columns I. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |α(τ)| ≤ |α| (Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2}, and by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(A_I)² = det(AAᵀ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = 1. Hence |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E. The covector α_τ(v_1, …, v_n) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} satisfies α_τ(e_I) = det(A_I); hence ⟨α, α_τ⟩_E = α(τ) for every α, |α_τ| = 1 and α_τ(τ) = 1. (For n = 0 everything is trivial: α(τ) = α(∅) and |α| = |α(∅)|.)
2. (Consequences on M.) Let J : E* → E be the Riesz isomorphism (⟨α, J(η)⟩_E = η(α)) and β := J ∘ ξ, an Hⁿ⌞M-measurable E-valued map. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M we have ξ(x) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) with τ orthonormal, so by step 1: |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α ∈ E, β(x) = ±α_τ, |β(x)| = 1 and ⟨β(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 1.
3. (Integrability.) For every compact K ⊆ U, μ_R(K) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞. If ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), then tsupport ω is a compact subset of U and |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ (sup|ω|)·θ·1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, so the integrand is integrable and T(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R.
4. (Upper bound.) Let ω be admissible: ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω| ≤ 1. For Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1, and ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 0 if x ∉ W. Hence T(ω) ≤ ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ = μ_R(W), so max(T(ω), 0) ≤ μ_R(W). Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
5. (Lower bound: reduction to compact sets.) V := U ∩ W is open and μ_R(W) = μ_R(V) since M ⊆ U. V is the increasing union of the compact sets K_i := {x ∈ V : |x| ≤ i, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ V) ≥ 1/i} (K_i := {|x| ≤ i} if V = ℝ^P), so μ_R(V) = sup_i μ_R(K_i). It therefore suffices to prove M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for every compact K ⊆ V and every η > 0. Fix K and η; if μ_R(K) = 0 there is nothing to prove.
6. (Open neighbourhood.) Choose δ > 0 with {x : dist(x, K) ≤ 2δ} ⊆ V. The sets O_s := {x : dist(x, K) < s}, 0 < s ≤ δ, have compact closures contained in V ⊆ U, so μ_R(O_δ) < ∞ and μ_R(O_s) ↓ μ_R(K) as s ↓ 0 (continuity from above; K is closed). Fix s ∈ (0, δ] with μ_R(O ∖ K) < η, where O := O_s.
7. (Lusin.) μ_R⌞K is a finite Borel measure on a compact metric space and β is μ_R-measurable; by Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01/Lusin.lean) there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that β|K' is continuous; by inner regularity we may also assume that |β| = 1 and ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1 at every point of K' (these hold μ_R-a.e. by step 2).
8. (Continuous extension.) By Tietze's extension theorem (applied to the coordinates of β in a basis of E), β|K' extends to a continuous g_0 : ℝ^P → E. Let r : E → E be the radial retraction r(α) := α if |α| ≤ 1, r(α) := α/|α| otherwise (continuous, |r| ≤ 1, r = id on the closed unit ball). By Urysohn's lemma choose a continuous χ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ = 1 on K' and tsupport χ ⊆ O compact. Put g := χ·(r ∘ g_0). Then g is continuous, tsupport g ⊆ O is compact, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere, and g = β on K'.
9. (Smoothing.) Let φ_σ (σ > 0) be a standard mollifier (smooth, ≥ 0, ∫φ_σ = 1, supported in the closed σ-ball) and g_σ := g * φ_σ (componentwise convolution). Then g_σ is C^∞, tsupport g_σ ⊆ {x : dist(x, tsupport g) ≤ σ} ⊆ O for 0 < σ < dist(tsupport g, ℝ^P ∖ O), |g_σ(x)| ≤ ∫ |g(x − y)| φ_σ(y) dy ≤ 1 (convexity of the norm), and g_σ → g uniformly as σ ↓ 0 (g is uniformly continuous). Viewed as an n-form, g_σ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (compact support in O ⊆ U) and g_σ is admissible for M_W(T) (O ⊆ V ⊆ W, |g_σ| ≤ 1).
10. (Estimate.) By steps 2–3, |T(g_σ) − ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R| ≤ sup|g_σ − g|·μ_R(closure O) → 0 as σ ↓ 0. On K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ = ⟨β, ξ⟩ = 1; on O ∖ K', ⟨g, ξ⟩ ≥ −|g| ≥ −1 μ_R-a.e.; off O, g = 0. Hence ∫⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ μ_R(K') − μ_R(O ∖ K') ≥ (μ_R(K) − η) − (μ_R(O ∖ K) + μ_R(K ∖ K')) ≥ μ_R(K) − 3η. Therefore max(T(g_σ), 0) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η for σ small, and M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(K) − 4η.
11. By step 5, M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞); together with step 4, M_W(T) = μ_R(W). ∎
Remark (reuse; not a proof step). Step 4 proves M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W) and steps 5–11 prove μ_R(W) ≤ M_W(T) for open W. subproblems.statement: For all P, n: (1) for every n-covector α on ℝ^P and v_1, …, v_n ∈ ℝ^P, |α(v_1, …, v_n)| ≤ |α|_E·(det(v_i·v_j)_{i,j})^{1/2}, where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{i_1<⋯<i_n} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15; (2) for every orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n in ℝ^P there is an n-covector α with |α|_E ≤ 1 and α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1.

Source: Simon 6.1 (Λ^n with the inner product making e^{i_1}∧⋯∧e^{i_n} orthonormal, 6.1.15) and 6.3.4–3.5 (|v_1∧⋯∧v_n| = J); these are the algebraic facts behind "M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W}θ dH^n" (6.3.2(3)) and the Jacobian bound in step 5 of the parent proof.
1. Notation. 𝓘 := the strictly increasing maps I : Fin n → Fin P; e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k; for I ∈ 𝓘, α_I := α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I n}); by definition |α|_E = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I²)^{1/2} (the sum over all I with the StrictMono filter). For v = (v_1, …, v_n) let V be the P×n matrix V_{k,j} := ⟨e_k, v_j⟩ = v_j(k), and for I ∈ 𝓘 let V_I be the n×n matrix (V_I)_{a,j} := v_j(I a).
2. Expansion. α(v) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I·det V_I. Proof: write v_j = Σ_k v_j(k)e_k and expand by multilinearity: α(v) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_j v_j(f j))·α(e_{f 1}, …, e_{f n}). Terms with f not injective vanish (α alternating, repeated argument). Each injective f is uniquely f = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 (the increasing enumeration of its range) and σ a permutation, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)α_I. So α(v) = Σ_I α_I Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j v_j(I(σ j)) = Σ_I α_I det V_I by the Leibniz formula.
3. Cauchy–Binet. Σ_{I∈𝓘} (det V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. Proof: det(VᵀV) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i (Σ_k V_{k,i}V_{k,σ i}) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i V_{f i, i})·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{f i, σ i} = Σ_f (Π_i V_{f i, i})·det(V_f), where V_f is the n×n matrix (V_{f a, j})_{a,j}. det V_f = 0 unless f is injective, and for f = I∘σ, det V_f = sgn(σ) det V_I (row permutation). Hence det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det V_I·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{I(σ i), i} = Σ_I (det V_I)² (Leibniz formula again).
4. Part (1). By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘, |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}(Σ_I (det V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩))^{1/2} by step 3 (the Gram determinant is ≥ 0, being a sum of squares).
5. Part (2). For n = 0 take α the constant 0-covector with value 1: |α|_E = 1 (𝓘 consists of the empty map) and α() = 1. For n ≥ 1 let α(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}; it is multilinear, alternating and continuous, hence an n-covector, and α(τ) = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1. Moreover α_I = det(⟨τ_a, e_{I b}⟩)_{a,b} = det(T_I) with T the P×n matrix of τ (transposes have equal determinants), so by step 3 applied to v = τ: |α|_E² = Σ_I det(T_I)² = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = 1. Hence |α|_E = 1 ≤ 1.
6. Degenerate cases are covered: if n > P then 𝓘 = ∅, |α|_E = 0, every n-covector vanishes (n vectors in ℝ^P are dependent) and there is no orthonormal n-family.
proof_key_steps: Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I) det V_I by multilinearity and alternation.
Cauchy–Binet: Σ_I (det V_I)² = det(v_i·v_j).
Cauchy–Schwarz gives (1); the covector u ↦ det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩) gives (2).

(b) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open, R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U (contract structure) and E is Borel, then (M ∩ E, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U and it represents some current in 𝒟_n(U). (c) If U is open and A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) are integer multiplicity (contract IsIntegerMultiplicity), then so is A − B. Source: Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the density argument in the proof of Theorem 1.6 “⇒” (chapter-03.txt lines 107–160); Ch. 6, Remarks 3.2(1) and 2.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 287–293, 755–768), stated in the book without proof; and Ch. 6, Remark 2.6 for the orientation bound. Hⁿ := μHE[n] throughout. For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap). The statement has four parts: (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction of a representation to a Borel set, (c) differences of integer multiplicity currents, (d) the orientation bound |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α|; U is open in (a)–(c).

Preliminaries.
(P0) Normalization: SimonGMT's density theorems are stated for simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n, which equals μHE[n] for natural n (SimonGMT Chapter02 simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, with simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure); hence null sets, finiteness and densities transfer verbatim, and Hⁿ is Borel regular (every set has a Borel hull of the same measure).
(P1) Scaling: for every set A, Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (Mathlib Measure.hausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and invariance of Hausdorff measure under isometries). Hence for Borel A and bounded Borel f, ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} f dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_A f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y).
(P2) Density zero (SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_6, for the Borel regular outer measure Hⁿ, cf. simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff): if D is Borel with Hⁿ(D) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∉ D, lim_{r↓0} Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ) = 0.
(P3) Cauchy–Binet. For n×P matrices A, B, det(ABᵀ) = Σ_I det(A_I) det(B_I), the sum over increasing I = (i_1 < ⋯ < i_n) in {1, …, P}, A_I the n×n submatrix of columns I. Proof: the j-th column of ABᵀ is Σ_k B_{jk}A_{·k}, so by multilinearity det(ABᵀ) = Σ_{k_1,…,k_n} B_{1k_1}⋯B_{nk_n} det(A_{·k_1}, …, A_{·k_n}); terms with a repeated index vanish, and grouping the remaining tuples by their underlying increasing tuple I (k = I ∘ σ for a permutation σ) gives Σ_I det(A_I) Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j B_{j, I_{σ(j)}} = Σ_I det(A_I)det(B_I). (For n > P both sides are 0 — no increasing I, and rank ABᵀ < n.)
(P4) Orientation bound. If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal in ℝ^P and ⟨α, ζ⟩ = ±α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors α, then |⟨α, ζ⟩| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm). Proof: with A_{ik} := ⟨τ_i, e_k⟩, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_I det(A_I) α(e_I); by Cauchy–Schwarz and (P3), |α(τ)| ≤ |α|(Σ_I det(A_I)²)^{1/2} = |α| det(AAᵀ)^{1/2} = |α|, since AAᵀ = (⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) is the identity. For n = 0, |α(∅)| = |α|.
(P5) Two unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q differ by a sign: if τ, τ' are orthonormal bases of Q, τ'_i = Σ_j O_{ij}τ_j with O orthogonal, and α(τ') = det(O)α(τ) = ±α(τ) for every alternating α. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q and IsUnitOrientationOf ζ' Q imply ζ' = ζ or ζ' = −ζ, and IsUnitOrientationOf (−ζ) Q holds whenever IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q.
(P6) If R = (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in an open U, then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (θ ≥ 1 on M).

(d) Orientation bound. By the orientation field of an IMRep, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ R.carrier there is Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ with ⟨α, R.orient x⟩ = ±α(τ) for all α; by (P4), |R.orient x α| ≤ |α| for all α. (No openness of U is needed.)

(a) Locality. Let U be open, M ⊆ M' ⊆ U Borel with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and D := M' ∖ M.
1. For R ∈ ℕ let U_R := {x ∈ U : |x| < R, infDist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/R} (U_R := {|x| < R} if U = ℝ^P). U_R is open, closure(U_R) is a compact subset of U, and U_R ↑ U. D_R := D ∩ U_R is Borel with Hⁿ(D_R) ≤ Hⁿ(M' ∩ closure(U_R)) < ∞. By (P2) there is an Hⁿ-null set Z_R such that every x ∉ D_R ∪ Z_R satisfies Hⁿ(D_R ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ) as r ↓ 0. Let Z := ⋃_R Z_R, and let Z' ⊇ Z be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0). Let x ∈ M ∖ Z'; choose R with x ∈ U_R and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{r₀}(x) ⊆ U_R. Then x ∉ D_R (as x ∈ M) and D ∩ B̄_r(x) = D_R ∩ B̄_r(x) for r < r₀, so Hⁿ(D ∩ B̄_r(x)) = o(rⁿ).
2. Fix such x, a subspace Q and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_ρ(0). For r < r₀/ρ the sets η_{x,r}(M), η_{x,r}(M') meet B_ρ(0) in sets of finite Hⁿ-measure, so the integrals below are genuine Bochner integrals. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(M') is the disjoint union of η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(D), and by (P1)
 |∫_{η_{x,r}(M')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dHⁿ| ≤ |f|_∞ r^{−n} Hⁿ(D ∩ B_{rρ}(x)) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
Hence for every f the two families of integrals have the same limit as r → 0⁺ or both have none; the condition finrank Q = n is common to both predicates. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q for every x ∈ M ∖ Z' and every Q; the exceptional set M ∩ Z' is null for Hⁿ⌞M. ∎

(b) Restriction. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in the open set U and E a Borel set. Define R' with carrier M ∩ E and the same mult θ and orient ξ.
1. Structure fields: M ∩ E is Borel and contained in U; countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and θ > 0 on M ∩ E; ∫_{M∩E∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ E) ≤ Hⁿ⌞M.
2. Orientation: by (P6) and (a) applied to M ∩ E ⊆ M ⊆ U, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ E and all Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (M ∩ E) x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. With the orientation field of R (Hⁿ-a.e. on M) this gives the orientation field of R'.
3. The current: A(ω) := ∫_{M∩E} θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). By (d), |θ⟨ω, ξ⟩| ≤ |ω|_∞ θ 1_{tsupport ω} Hⁿ-a.e. on M, and tsupport ω is a compact subset of U, so the integrand is integrable; A is linear. If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges: supports in a fixed compact K ⊆ U and uniform convergence of all derivatives, in particular |ω_j|_∞ → 0 since all norms on the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors are equivalent), then |A(ω_j)| ≤ |ω_j|_∞ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ → 0. So A is a GeometricCurrentOn U n and R' represents A (IMRep.Represents, IMRep.action). ∎

(c) Differences. Let A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), U open, be represented by R_A = (M_A, θ_A, ξ_A) and R_B = (M_B, θ_B, ξ_B).
1. (Borel versions and good points.) Choose Borel ξ̃_A, ξ̃_B equal to ξ_A, ξ_B Hⁿ-a.e. on M_A, resp. M_B (a.e. strong measurability; set them 0 off the carriers). Let G be the set of x ∈ M_A ∪ M_B such that: if x ∈ M_A, then ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x) and there is Q_A(x) with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M_A x Q_A(x) and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_A x) Q_A(x); the analogous condition for B if x ∈ M_B; and, for each pair (N, N') among (M_A ∩ M_B, M_A), (M_A ∩ M_B, M_B) with x ∈ N, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q for every Q. By the orientation fields of R_A, R_B, by (P6) and by (a), (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; let N₀ ⊇ (M_A ∪ M_B) ∖ G be a Borel Hⁿ-null set (P0).
2. (Overlap.) Let x ∈ (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀. The approximate tangent space of M_A ∩ M_B at x exists and equals Q_A(x) and also Q_B(x) (the equivalences defining G and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces, SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique); so Q_A(x) = Q_B(x) and by (P5) ξ̃_B(x) = ε(x)ξ̃_A(x) with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. Put ε(x) := 1 if ξ̃_B(x) = ξ̃_A(x) and ε(x) := −1 otherwise (a Borel function).
3. (Data.) Put O := (M_A ∩ M_B) ∖ N₀, k := θ_A − εθ_B ∈ ℤ on O, and
 M := ((M_A ∖ M_B) ∪ (M_B ∖ M_A) ∪ {x ∈ O : k(x) ≠ 0}) ∖ N₀,
 θ := θ_A on M_A ∖ M_B, θ_B on M_B ∖ M_A, |k| on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel, ℕ-valued),
 ζ := ξ̃_A on M_A ∖ M_B, −ξ̃_B on M_B ∖ M_A, sign(k)ξ̃_A on O, 0 elsewhere (Borel).
For every x ∉ N₀: θ(x)1_M(x)ζ(x) = θ_A(x)1_{M_A}(x)ξ̃_A(x) − θ_B(x)1_{M_B}(x)ξ̃_B(x) (on O with k = 0 both sides vanish; on O with k ≠ 0, θ_Aξ̃_A − θ_Bεξ̃_A = kξ̃_A = |k| sign(k)ξ̃_A; the other cases are immediate).
4. (Representation.) For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), integrating ⟨ω, ·⟩ against both sides of step 3 (N₀ is null; all integrands are integrable by (d), since θ1_M ≤ θ_A1_{M_A} + θ_B1_{M_B}):
 ∫_M θ⟨ω, ζ⟩ dHⁿ = ∫_{M_A} θ_A⟨ω, ξ_A⟩ dHⁿ − ∫_{M_B} θ_B⟨ω, ξ_B⟩ dHⁿ = A(ω) − B(ω) = (A − B)(ω).
5. (Structure fields.) M is Borel, M ⊆ M_A ∪ M_B ⊆ U, and M is countably n-rectifiable (countablyRectifiable_iUnion, CountablyRectifiable.mono). θ is Borel and ℕ-valued with θ ≥ 1 on M (|k| ≥ 1 where k ≠ 0), and ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M_A∩K} θ_A dHⁿ + ∫_{M_B∩K} θ_B dHⁿ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
6. (Orientation.) For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M_A ∩ K) + Hⁿ(M_B ∩ K) < ∞ by (P6) applied to R_A, R_B. Apply (a) to the pairs (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M_A), (M ∩ M_A ⊆ M), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M_B), (M ∩ M_B ⊆ M) (all Borel, contained in U, with locally finite Hⁿ-measure): for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ M_A the approximate tangent spaces of M and of M_A at x coincide (both equal that of M ∩ M_A), and similarly for M_B. Let x be such a point, x ∉ N₀. If x ∈ M_A, then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_A(x) and ζ(x) = ±ξ_A(x) (cases M_A ∖ M_B and O, using ξ̃_A(x) = ξ_A(x)), a unit orientation of Q_A(x) by (P5). If x ∈ M_B ∖ M_A, ζ(x) = −ξ_B(x) is a unit orientation of Q_B(x), the approximate tangent space of M at x. Hence the orientation field holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M.
So (M, θ, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing A − B, and A − B is integer multiplicity. ∎

Consequences used by siblings. (i) By (c), 0 = B − B, −B = 0 − B and A + B := A − (0 − B) are integer multiplicity whenever A, B are, hence so is every finite integer combination of integer multiplicity currents in an open set. subproblems.title: Support lemma (Simon 6.2.11): a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support (reuse of the accepted declaration dtc_vanish_off_support)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, where spt S = U ∖ Z_S and Z_S is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Then S(ω) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dtc_vanish_off_support (node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1, accepted candidate commit 44ef61f79e2168134f8a5a6d6520baba56052d67) with the identical frozen Lean type; no new child worker is provisioned. Its accepted parent-supplied proof is reproduced verbatim below.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of the zero region of S, hence covered by finitely many open sets on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.
